title: Joe Oliver as a pool player, the Lincoln Garden fire and Lee Collins
summary: Talk about Oliver's pool playing, Giannis Censier, the Lincoln Garden fire that stopped Jackson joining Oliver, and Lee Collins' Sidewalk Blues.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I was talking about Oliver all day. Joe Oliver was a good pool player as I told you.
Oh yeah, he used to play with him.
You're a good pool player too.
You can catch him by one o'clock every day.
Well there's a fella Giannis Censier, you run into Giannis Censier?
Oh yes, I've known him. He's a nice fella.
Yeah, he was with that hot five.
He's in California now. Oh he's in California now.

Yeah, he's a plaster or something. Yeah, I saw him last time I was in y'all, he was making plenty of money. He was doing a whole lot of building there. Now Giannis Censier, he came up later on. Now when these two boys, Albert, this big guard, now they call him Bonnie, you know they call him Bonnie, see? And Albert, Albert, that's Albert in French, you understand? And so I saw them there, Rudy Richards was the other saxophone player with Joe Oliver at the Lincoln Garden. I was at the Lincoln Garden the night that the place caught fire. Oh really? Yeah. A fella flew around there to match and set the place on fire. That's what happened. I was supposed to join Joe Oliver. That's why I didn't join him, because the place caught on fire. Mrs. Majors was the proprietor. They had a fella by the name of Bud Redd, who was the manager. And old King Jones, the fella who used to spiel in front of the survive when they had the
fights, he was the instructor back there.

Yeah, well he was a regular fashion player. Twenty-five or thirty suits of clothes. They'd give him suits of clothes just to advertise. I heard he died not so long ago in New York. And getting back to, well Lee played with Joe Oliver at the Lincoln Garden too, see? Well now the Sidewalk Blues, Lee wrote the Sidewalk Blues and Jellie Roten, turned it over to Jellie Roten and Jellie Roten had it to copyright it. And that was the last, that was the last, maybe Lee told you about it.
But Lee never did talk about it?
